label: first copy step (input = first token n/t), sparse and content-dependent
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.015% of steps). 75% of activation mass is at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1, input = first original token), almost entirely when that first token is n or t (also m/o/j/v more weakly). Within that slot it fires on only ~1.6% of eligible steps; firing is enriched for short sequences (L 4-6), second token v/o/u, and digits (esp. 3) or h early in the sequence (top examples: n v 3 3 h l, t v 3 2 3, n o 3 3 3), but no simple conjunction exceeded F1 ~0.16. The remaining ~24% of mass is weak original-phase activations at t = 3-5, usually following h/y/3 tokens. Never fires at t < 3 or at recall_idx >= 2. Magnitude is highest at the recall_idx==1 step for n/t-initial sequences with v/o second and 3s following.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=y (+4.18), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=t (+3.67), in_tok=n (+3.33), orig1=v (+3.29), in_tok=m (+3.09), orig2=3 (+2.97). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.69), orig_idx=-1 (-2.50), orig2=s (-2.27), L=9 (-1.31).
